page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with two threads per core. The underlying hardware utilizes an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at a base frequency of 2.9 GHz, supported by 48 KB L1 data cache per core, 1 MB L2 cache per core, and a 48 MB shared L3 cache. It is provisioned with 32.0 GB of memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, and it connects via a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark results for ecs.g7se.2xlarge exhibit middle-tier compute and memory capabilities consistent with its 8-vCPU allocation. In synthetic evaluation, stress-ng yields 1858.18 for single-core and 7750.15 for multi-core, while Geekbench registers 1517.0 in single-core and 5658.0 in multi-core metrics. Memory performance reaches 58.09 GB/sec read and 38.1 GB/sec write throughput over uncached 256 MB blocks. Hardware support for AVX-512 VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI aids vector calculations and cryptographic operations, achieving 7302.21 points in PassMark CPU encryption tests.

The compute profile reflects balanced execution across standard workloads, highlighted by static web serving throughput of 11.25 GB/sec and 7.88 million Redis SET operations per second. However, architectural tradeoffs appear when targeting larger memory-intensive or parameter-heavy applications. LLM inference benchmarks with a medium 7B parameter model register only 15.66 prompt tokens per second and 6.62 generation tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated acceleration and standard memory bandwidth ceilings.

Without local storage and bundled public IPv4 addresses, the instance relies on remote network-attached block volumes. Qualitatively, the ecs.g7se.2xlarge presents a predictable cost-efficiency model for enterprise application tiers that require stable, dedicated x86 CPU allocations and balanced memory ratios without the overhead of unused accelerator hardware. Typical workload fits include web serving tiers, software compilation pipelines, middle-tier enterprise backends, and caching systems.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.2xlarge is an x86_64 general-purpose server powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at 2.9 GHz. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 32.0 GB of RAM, and a 3 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance does not bundle local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network storage configurations. Benchmark evaluation reflects standard mid-range results across compute and memory operations, including 1517.0 single-core and 5658.0 multi-core scores in Geekbench, alongside 7.88 million Redis SET operations per second and 11.25 GB/sec static web throughput. AVX-512 and cryptographic instruction sets like VAES provide acceleration for encryption and vector processing. Due to modest single-node memory bandwidth and absent discrete accelerators, larger language model processing remains limited. The configuration offers balanced efficiency suited for web application serving, software compilation, caching, and enterprise application backends.
